c.tagline: Sunlit coast, paella, and futuristic architecture.

emergency.note: 091 national police, 092 local police and 061 health emergencies also work; 112 operators usually offer English.

hood_landmark.Ciutat Vella: Valencia Cathedral with its climbable Miguelete bell tower
hood_landmark.Ruzafa (Russafa): Mercado de Ruzafa, the colorful modernist market hall
hood_landmark.El Carmen: Torres de Serranos, the medieval city gate
hood_landmark.El Cabanyal: colorful tiled fishermen's houses steps from Malvarrosa beach
hood_landmark.Eixample: Mercado de Colón, the ornate modernista market

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing on Malvarrosa beach, in the centre and around the stations

hood_desc: Ciutat Vella is the historic old town and tourist heart, home to the cathedral, Plaza de la Reina and the Central Market, ideal for first-time visitors who want landmarks and museums within walking distance.
Ruzafa (Russafa) is the trendy, bohemian district packed with cafes, vintage shops, tapas bars and nightlife, perfect for younger travelers, foodies and creatives who want a hip local scene.
El Carmen is the oldest medieval quarter with narrow winding streets, street art and lively bars, best suited to nightlife lovers and those seeking an artsy, atmospheric stay.
El Cabanyal is the colorful former fishermen quarter beside the beach, increasingly hip with great seafood and tiled houses, great for beach lovers wanting an authentic, less touristy neighborhood.
Eixample is an elegant, upscale grid district with modernist architecture, refined restaurants and a calm residential feel, suited to travelers who want a quieter, sophisticated base near the center.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: Rides use the rechargeable SUMA10 smartcard, sold and topped up at metro/tram machines and EMT points; contactless bank cards are not yet accepted at the gates, only Metrovalencia's own smartcards. A single ticket costs from €1.50 for one zone up to €4.80 for the widest zone (about $1.65-5.30), and a 1-day SUMA T pass starts at €4 (about $4.40).
transit.hours: Metro and trams run from around 5:30am until about midnight (some lines finish nearer 11pm); EMT buses run through the evening, with a handful of Nitbus night lines on Friday and Saturday nights.

transit.m: Metro line 3/5 to Xativa or Colon, 25 min
Bus line 150 to city center, 40-45 min
